# Overview {.unnumbered}

Harvard's TinyTorch is to machine learning systems as MIT's xv6 is to operating systems: a compact, readable reference implementation in which every layer of the modern deep learning stack is built from first principles and can be read in full.

Building a system creates understanding that using one never does. In this book we move beyond calling library functions (`import torch`) and construct a working deep learning runtime from first principles, from memory layout and automatic differentiation through multi-head attention to quantization and the KV cache.

| Part | Focus | What you build |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Part I: The Core Engine** | Memory, gradients, optimization | `Tensor`, activations, `Linear`, `CrossEntropyLoss`, `DataLoader`, autograd, `AdamW`, the training loop |
| **Part II: Deep Architectures** | Images, text, transformers | `Conv2d`, `BPETokenizer`, `Embedding`, `MultiHeadAttention`, `TransformerBlock`, a small GPT |
| **Part III: Systems & Acceleration** | Measuring and speeding up | The roofline model, INT8 quantization, pruning and low-rank compression, fused kernels, `KVCache`, benchmarking, the capstone stack |
| **Part IV: Extensions & Future Frontiers** | Beyond TinyTorch | Triton kernels, compilers, and custom silicon |

: The four parts of TinyTorch and what each one builds. {#tbl-overview-parts tbl-colwidths="[28,24,48]"}

Everything in TinyTorch is written in Python on top of NumPy, with no other machine learning dependency. Every module ships with unit tests, and every chapter ends with a bridge from the minimal implementation to what production frameworks such as PyTorch do, and why.
